newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES SOFTER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES SOFTER ON IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar finished Tuesday's interbank session easier against hard currencies on the back of slight import pressure, exchange dealers said.
"We had a couple of ups and downs today but it was a very quiet market on the whole," one dealer commented.

He said the local unit peaked at 10.6700/6900 versus the key U.S. dollar after a few banks secured some export receipts which they sold to the market, but slipped again on increased foreign currency demand by importers.

He and other dealers were however all agreed that the four-week stalemate between the government and junior doctors and nurses striking for better salaries and working conditions had not affected the market.
"Our market is driven by supply and demand...it doesn't respond to anything else really," said one.
The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Tuesday at 10.6750/6950 against the U.S. dollar, slightly down from 10.6725/6925 overnight and was quoted at 17.8700/9140 from 17.7900/8100 against pound sterling.
It also slipped to 7.1000/1150 from 7.0890/1025 versus the mark and to 2.2990/3060 against South Africa's rand from 2.2880/2950, tracking a weaker U.S. dollar against those currencies overseas.
